provenance.pipeline: satsuki v1 (v1.0.1 editorial re-edit: usage-note reshaping corpus-wide, lane discrimination for same-surface families, against prompts/style.md)

patterns.usage_note: Gives the cause or reason for what the main clause reports, following a plain-form clause, past or non-past, or a noun plus の (混雑が予想されるため, 大雪のため). The sibling entry is the purpose ため, which takes a non-past volitional verb (合格するために勉強する), so volitionality decides the reading with a non-past clause. It states the reason as objective fact and suits announcements and written notices, where から and ので sound chattier.

examples.ruby: 大雪[おおゆき]のため、明日[あす]の試合[しあい]は中止[ちゅうし]になりました。
examples.english: Owing to the heavy snow, tomorrow's match has been called off.

examples.ruby: 電車[でんしゃ]が遅[おく]れたため、会議[かいぎ]に間[ま]に合[あ]わなかった。
examples.english: Because the train was delayed, I was unable to make the meeting.

examples.ruby: 工事[こうじ]のため、来週[らいしゅう]はプールが使[つか]えません。
examples.english: Because of construction work, the pool is closed next week.

patterns.usage_note: Pins a bad turn on one small, often trivial cause, so it comes wrapped in regret or self-reproach and the outcome is out of all proportion to it (値段だけで選ぶばっかりに壊れる). だけに draws a reasonable, sometimes admiring conclusion from its cause; ばかりに only blames. A past-form verb before it points at a single misstep, a non-past adjective or habitual verb at a standing trait behind repeated trouble; ばっかりに is the emphatic spoken doubling.

examples.ruby: 値段[ねだん]だけで靴[くつ]を選[えら]ぶばっかりに、いつも一週間[いっしゅうかん]で壊[こわ]れる。
examples.english: Just because I pick shoes on price alone, they always fall apart within a week.

examples.ruby: 人[ひと]が良[よ]すぎるばっかりに、あいつは何度[なんど]も騙[だま]される。
examples.english: Just because he's too good-natured for his own good, he keeps getting taken in over and over.

examples.ruby: 何[なん]でも一人[ひとり]で抱[かか]え込[こ]むばっかりに、いつも体[からだ]を壊[こわ]す。
examples.english: Simply because she shoulders everything alone, she always ends up making herself ill.

glosses: precisely because; all the more because
patterns.usage_note: Presents the second clause as the conclusion its cause makes obvious, often with an added "all the more so" (期待していただけに残念だ). The outcome may be welcome or unwelcome; ばかりに by contrast apportions blame for a bad result, and ため only reports the link rather than asking the hearer to agree it is natural. It attaches straight to a bare noun (プロだけに); the close sibling だけあって is limited to results that live up to the cause.

examples.ruby: 値段[ねだん]が高[たか]いだけに、作[つく]りがしっかりしている。
examples.english: It's expensive, and sure enough it's solidly built.

examples.ruby: 元[もと]プロだけに、フォームがまるで違[ちが]う。
examples.english: He's a former pro, and it shows: his form is on another level.

examples.ruby: 毎年[まいとし]優勝[ゆうしょう]しているだけに、周[まわ]りの期待[きたい]も大[おお]きい。
examples.english: They win it every year, which makes the expectations around them all the heavier.
